source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.15 (pp. 649-652): seismic design of nonstructural components permanently attached to structures, their supports and attachments
name: Seismic design of nonstructural components

force.note: Eq 6.2.57 prints ah = 0.67 Z S; Sec 2.5.13.2 has (2/3) Z S. The printed 0.67 is used (owner rule: the more conservative of the two, 0.5 % higher).
force.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.15.3, Eq 6.2.57 (p. 651): Fc = αc ah Wc Ic / Rc × (1 + 2 z/h), 0.75 ah Wc Ic ≤ Fc ≤ 1.5 ah Wc Ic, ah = 0.67 Z S, z/h ≤ 1, z ≥ 0; applied in two orthogonal horizontal directions with a concurrent vertical ± 0.5 ah Wc

importance.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.15.1 (p. 650): Ic = 1.5 for a component required to function after an earthquake, containing hazardous materials, or in or attached to an occupancy category IV building and needed for its continued operation; else 1.0

defaults.note: SAEngine practice, not BNBC: how a drawn item maps to a table row when none is chosen. An interior wall defaults to plain (unreinforced) masonry, the lowest Rc of the interior walls (conservative); a wall on the top story with no story above is a cantilever parapet; a structural wall's out-of-plane anchorage force uses the exterior nonstructural wall row; an overhead water tank is an atmospheric tank (wet-side row).

exemptions.label: Architectural components in Category B with Ic = 1.0, other than parapets supported by bearing or shear walls
Mechanical and electrical components in Category B
Mechanical and electrical components in Category C with Ic = 1.0
Mechanical and electrical components in Category D with Ic = 1.0 and either flexible connections, or mounted at most 1.2 m above the floor and weighing at most 1780 N
Mechanical and electrical components in Category C or D with Ic = 1.0, flexible connections, and weighing at most 89 N (distribution systems at most 73 N/m)

interaction.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.15 (p. 650): where supported components with periods over 0.06 s weigh more than 25 % of the total seismic weight W, the structure is designed with the interaction between the structure and the components

isolation.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Table 6.2.23 note b (p. 657): components on vibration isolators have a bumper restraint or snubber in each horizontal direction; the design force is 2 Fc where the nominal clearance (air gap) exceeds 6 mm, else Fc

connections.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 1.7.3.2(b) (pp. 503-504): exterior nonbearing panels; joints and connections allow a relative storey movement of at least 2 × the storey drift under wind or design seismic forces, or 12 mm; bodies of connections for 1.33 × the force of Sec 2.5.15, fasteners for 4 ×

anchorage.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 1.7.3.6 (p. 504): concrete and masonry structural walls anchored to the floors and roof for the horizontal forces of Sec 2.4.11 and 2.5.15, at least 4.09 kN/m of wall; the wall is designed for bending between anchors spaced more than 1.2 m

relativeDisplacement.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.15.4, Eqs 6.2.58-6.2.61 (pp. 651-652): Dc = δxA − δyA ≤ (hx − hy) ΔaA / hsx on one structure; Dc = |δxA| + |δyB| ≤ hx ΔaA / hsx + hy ΔaB / hsx between two structures; Δa/hsx the allowable storey drift ratio (Table 6.2.21)

sources.components: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Table 6.2.22 (pp. 654-655) and Table 6.2.23 (pp. 656-657); note a: αc = 1.0 for rigid and rigidly attached components, 2.5 for flexible and flexibly attached ones, a lower αc (≥ 1.0) only by detailed dynamic analysis
sources.forceTransfer: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.15.2 (p. 650): positively fastened attachments, no friction from gravity, a continuous load path
sources.nonSeismic: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.15.3 (p. 651): where non-seismic loads on a component exceed Fc they govern the strength design; the seismic detailing still applies
